prompt: In envelope encryption, what does Cloud KMS encrypt?

choices.text: The bucket's metadata
choices.why: Metadata is not what envelope encryption is about.

choices.text: The data itself, object by object
choices.why: The data is encrypted locally with a DEK.

choices.text: Each object's data key
choices.why: Right. It wraps DEKs; the data never reaches it.

choices.text: Passwords stored in Secret Manager
choices.why: A different service, lesson 17.

prompt: What is stored beside the ciphertext in `order-1001.json`?

choices.text: A hash of the plain text
choices.why: Not stored; and it would leak information.

choices.text: The KEK itself
choices.why: The KEK would then be wherever the data is.

choices.text: The wrapped DEK and the KEK version
choices.why: Right. Enough to ask for an unwrap, nothing more.

choices.text: The DEK, so it can be decrypted quickly
choices.why: The plain DEK is never stored.

prompt: After a rotation, why does order-1001 still decrypt?

choices.text: Decryption ignores the version
choices.why: It reads the version from the file and uses it.

choices.text: Rotation re-encrypted it under version 2
choices.why: Nothing was re-encrypted.

choices.text: Version 1 still exists and wrapped its DEK
choices.why: Right. Rotation adds a version; it removes none.

choices.text: The DEK was cached in memory
choices.why: Each run is a new process; nothing is cached.

prompt: Version 1 is destroyed. The ciphertext of order-1001 is still on disk. What is it now?

choices.text: Unreadable noise, for everybody
choices.why: Right. Data made unrecoverable without touching it.

choices.text: Readable by Google support, on request
choices.why: A destroyed version is gone for Google too.

choices.text: Readable once the file is restored from backup
choices.why: The backup has the same ciphertext and the same missing key.

choices.text: Readable with version 2
choices.why: Version 2 never wrapped that DEK.

prompt: A São Paulo bucket is to use CMEK. Where must the key be?

choices.text: Anywhere, as long as the IAM is right
choices.why: Location matters as much as IAM.

choices.text: In southamerica-east1
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In the us multi-region, where KMS runs
choices.why: KMS runs in many locations.

choices.text: In global, so every region can use it
choices.why: A global key does not serve a regional bucket's CMEK.

prompt: Every write to the CMEK bucket fails after it is created. What is the likeliest missing piece?

choices.text: The Cloud Storage service agent's role on the key
choices.why: Right. Without encrypterDecrypter it cannot wrap.

choices.text: versioning on the bucket
choices.why: Writes do not depend on versioning.

choices.text: prevent_destroy on the key
choices.why: That is a Terraform guard, not a permission.

choices.text: An HSM protection level
choices.why: Software keys work for CMEK.

prompt: Why did the KMS plan stop with `401 Invalid Credentials` when earlier plans did not?
hint: What is read during a plan?

choices.text: KMS resources always need a real token
choices.why: The key ring and key were proposed fine.

choices.text: A data source must ask Google at plan time
choices.why: Right. Resources are only proposed; data sources are read.

choices.text: The configuration was invalid
choices.why: validate said it was valid.

choices.text: The fake token expired
choices.why: It was never valid to begin with.

choices.text: Automatic rotation
choices.why: Rotation is unaffected.

choices.text: Anybody destroying the key in the console
choices.why: It binds Terraform only.

choices.text: Disabling the key
choices.why: Disabling is a different operation.

choices.text: Terraform planning the key's destruction
choices.why: Right. Which would schedule every version for destruction.

prompt: A version is scheduled for destruction with the default period. What can still happen?

choices.text: It keeps encrypting new data until the end
choices.why: Scheduled versions are disabled.

choices.text: Nothing: it is destroyed at once
choices.why: Destruction waits for the scheduled period.

choices.text: It is free during the period
choices.why: Scheduled versions are active and billed.

choices.text: Cancelling it, within the window
choices.why: Right. restore leaves it disabled.

prompt: A software key rotated quarterly has four active versions after a year. At 0.06 USD per version a month, what does it cost a month?
A bucket was written for two years under a key rotated quarterly. Somebody wants to destroy the old versions to tidy up. What happens?
hint: Every version still wraps some objects.

choices.text: Objects written under them become unreadable
choices.why: Right. Never destroy an old version to tidy up.

choices.text: Cloud Storage re-encrypts the objects first
choices.why: Nothing re-encrypts automatically.

choices.text: Nothing: only the primary version matters
choices.why: Old objects are read through old versions.

choices.text: The bucket's encryption falls back to Google's keys
choices.why: There is no fallback for data already written.

prompt: Put a key version's states in the order it passes through them, from creation.
trap: Destroyed before scheduled is the slip: destruction always waits out the scheduled period.

prompt: Encryption with a key in your own Cloud KMS, used by a Google service, is called customer-managed encryption, or ___.
Which of these happened on your computer in this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Two orders encrypted under two key versions
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: An order made unreadable by deleting a version
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A key ring created in Cloud KMS
choices.why: No. Only planned.

choices.text: A 30-day destruction countdown
choices.why: No. The file was deleted at once.
